meta.title: Technology that changes what is possible
meta.subtitle: A WBG perspective on emerging capabilities and the builders to watch
meta.evidenceNote: Public-source research. WBG applications are editorial proposals; inclusion does not imply adoption or endorsement.
meta.coverageNote: The showcase highlights 63 distinct builders from the 102-profile landscape. Names rotate by topic to keep the radar readable.
meta.selectionRationale: Six development scenes connect technology to inclusive services, climate and agriculture, infrastructure, human capital, productive firms and energy. Four ITS scenes examine delivery, institutional workflows, evidence and control. Two frontier scenes examine scientific and physical AI where technical milestones could change development economics.
knownGaps: The film is a curated selection, not an exhaustive startup ranking or procurement shortlist.
Coverage of urban mobility, housing, waste and accessibility remains selective.
Country-level availability, implementation costs and measured outcomes need local validation.
Quantum computing and alternative AI hardware remain in the research landscape but are outside this two-minute narrative.

overview.title: From emerging capability to development value
overview.insight: A useful radar connects what is changing, who is building it and what evidence would make it worth pursuing.

sectors.label: AI & work
sectors.insight: Follow completed tasks, human effort and operational reliability.

sectors.label: Trust & data
sectors.insight: Preserve source evidence, permissions and accountable decisions.

sectors.label: Public services
sectors.insight: Design around languages, access barriers and usable public infrastructure.

sectors.label: Climate & Earth
sectors.insight: Connect observations to an action that someone can take.

sectors.label: Essential systems
sectors.insight: Improve the delivery of food, care, power and water.

sectors.label: Frontier systems
sectors.insight: Watch the milestones that could change the cost or feasibility of a task.

scenes.title: Public services in people's own language
scenes.claim: Local-language speech, phone-based AI and reusable public infrastructure widen the routes into digital services.
scenes.implication: Meet people in their language and channel, then connect the interaction to a service they can complete.
scenes.watch: Test comprehension, completion and exclusion across languages, devices and disability needs.

detail.opportunity: A voice interface becomes valuable when it helps someone complete an actual public-service task. Language models, identity services and interoperable public platforms address different parts of that journey and should be assessed together.
detail.proofToSeek: Check whether people understand the response and complete the task without additional help, including speakers poorly represented in training data. DIGIT and Mojaloop are public-good ecosystems; a deployed service also needs local operators, governance and accessible alternatives.
detail.firstExperiment: Choose one public information or application-support task in two local languages and test it with representative users. Compare completion, handoff failures and total cost against the existing channel while retaining a human route.

scenes.title: Climate signals that trigger action
scenes.claim: Weather, flood and crop intelligence can be connected to farm advice, operational triggers and risk protection.
scenes.implication: Turn better information into a timely decision for farmers, public agencies or resilience programs.
scenes.watch: Check warning lead time, missed events, local accuracy, farmer understanding and insurance basis risk.

detail.opportunity: The useful unit is an actionable decision: move supplies, inspect a field, change an agronomic intervention or trigger a predefined response. Forecasting and crop tools become more valuable when the person responsible, financing and delivery channel are already in place.
detail.proofToSeek: Reconstruct historical events using only the data that would have been available at the time and record false alarms as well as misses. For insurance, examine whether payouts track the losses farmers actually experience and whether exclusions are understood.
detail.firstExperiment: Select one district, one crop or hazard and one operational decision with a named owner. Run the new signal alongside the current process and document whether it changes the timing or quality of that decision.

scenes.title: Infrastructure you can verify
scenes.claim: Site imagery, satellite observations and sensor data make physical progress and infrastructure losses more visible.
scenes.implication: Direct scarce inspection and maintenance capacity to the gaps between reported progress and observable conditions.
scenes.watch: Validate flagged issues in the field; track useful findings per inspection and errors in location or timing.

detail.opportunity: Connect remote observations with project schedules, asset registers and local field evidence so teams can investigate discrepancies. This can support project supervision and utility maintenance while preserving the distinction between a detected anomaly and a confirmed problem.
detail.proofToSeek: Compare the system's priorities with independent field inspections and record missing, stale or mislocated observations. Satellite refresh intervals, sensor coverage and site-capture practices determine what the system can actually see.
detail.firstExperiment: Use one project corridor or a limited utility network area and predefine the conditions that warrant a visit. Measure confirmed findings per inspection and the time needed to assemble a defensible evidence packet.

scenes.title: Care and skills closer to people
scenes.claim: Digital tools support clinical workflows, foundational learning and the connection between skills and work.
scenes.implication: Strengthen the frontline worker, teacher and jobseeker's ability to act on useful information.
scenes.watch: Measure care, learning or job outcomes, with local validation and accountable professional oversight.

detail.opportunity: Better diagnostic support, clinic operations, teacher feedback and skills matching address different constraints on human capital. Their value depends on strengthening a functioning delivery pathway, including what happens after a risk, learning gap or skills need is identified.
detail.proofToSeek: For health, require clinical validation and applicable approvals for the intended population and workflow. For learning and employment, distinguish participation or engagement from measured learning gains, sustained placement and equitable access.
detail.firstExperiment: Choose one narrow pathway, such as teacher-supported mathematics practice or referral completion after screening. Agree an outcome measure with practitioners before comparing the new workflow with existing practice.

scenes.title: Digital tools for productive firms
scenes.claim: Payments, business software, device finance and trade data address different barriers to productive small firms.
scenes.implication: Connect technology access to better business operations, market participation and responsible financial services.
scenes.watch: Measure owner time, net costs and reliable market access; examine consumer protection and data portability.

detail.opportunity: Small firms need usable devices, payments, records and access to customers as well as finance. The WBG jobs strategy's emphasis on infrastructure, business conditions and capital provides a practical reason to examine these connected constraints.
detail.proofToSeek: Compare net fees, financing terms, reliability and time saved on the business owner's real tasks. Trade-data platforms require a separate check on coverage, linkage errors and what their network view omits, especially for smaller suppliers.
detail.firstExperiment: Follow a small cohort of firms through one operating workflow such as payments-to-reconciliation or booking-to-cash. Record setup effort, total recurring cost and whether the owner gains a more reliable view of the business.

scenes.title: Reliable power and better financing
scenes.claim: Distributed-energy software, payment models and risk analytics connect electricity operations with financing.
scenes.implication: Examine how better operating data and capital allocation can support affordable, reliable electricity access.
scenes.watch: Compare reliability, tariffs, maintenance capacity and portfolio risk at similar sites.

detail.opportunity: Energy-access programs need viable operations and affordable capital alongside physical assets. Distributed-energy operators, payment providers and infrastructure intelligence address complementary parts of reliability, affordability and service expansion.
detail.proofToSeek: Request comparable operating evidence on outages, utilization, collections and maintenance costs, with transparent tariff assumptions. Utility-risk analytics can support existing-network reliability; they do not by themselves establish that new households gained access.
detail.firstExperiment: Compare a small set of similar sites or feeders using operational and financial data already collected. Test whether a new forecast or risk ranking changes a maintenance or investment decision and improves its measured outcome.

scenes.title: From code suggestions to delivery
scenes.claim: Factory's November release connects agents with Azure, Azure DevOps and existing review controls.
scenes.implication: Test software agents against real maintenance work, with engineers judging the quality of the completed change.
scenes.watch: Track review effort, regressions, task completion, runtime cost and failures that need human recovery.

detail.opportunity: Software agents can be assessed on the complete path from a bounded issue to a tested, reviewable change. The 18 November Factory announcement adds a concrete Azure and Azure DevOps deployment example, while other builders illustrate agentic development and behavior-based modernization.
detail.proofToSeek: Count the engineer's time spent specifying, reviewing and correcting the work alongside agent runtime and cost. For legacy changes, use observed behavior and regression evidence to check that a successful build preserved the intended system behavior.
detail.firstExperiment: Select a small backlog of representative maintenance tasks in a non-production repository with known tests. Compare completion quality and total human effort across the existing workflow and one or two agent configurations.

scenes.title: From answers to accountable work
scenes.claim: Knowledge, connected tools and task execution combine in products and in emerging lean operating models.
scenes.implication: Redesign one institutional workflow around a completed outcome, explicit permissions and an accountable human owner.
scenes.watch: Count human edits, retries, exceptions and total cost for one fully completed deliverable.

detail.opportunity: Connect institutional context with a bounded sequence of actions and a defined finished artifact, such as a source-linked portfolio briefing. Seekr, Syntes, Glean, Dust and n8n offer different building blocks; Ravenopus is a company-described single-operator service model to examine through a completed deliverable.
detail.proofToSeek: Inspect source permissions, task state, human interventions and recovery when a tool fails or data changes. Ravenopus's operating model and performance are vendor-described, and should be evaluated through evidence of the work and its full economics.
detail.firstExperiment: Map one recurring task from its trigger through the final reviewed output and establish a manual baseline. Run a bounded agent workflow beside it, recording every human intervention and any action that exceeded its intended scope.

scenes.title: Turn documents into traceable evidence
scenes.claim: Document APIs preserve tables, fields and source locations for downstream search and AI workflows.
scenes.implication: Make project reports and supervisory records easier to compare, with material claims tied to their source evidence.
scenes.watch: Check the value, unit, period and source page; verify permissions and the actual deployment boundary.

detail.opportunity: Preserving document structure makes it easier to inspect the evidence behind a reported indicator or briefing claim. Parsing, retrieval, models and deployment controls are separate parts of the solution and should be compared on the actual document and language mix.
detail.proofToSeek: Test scanned pages, difficult tables, multilingual text and revisions against a reviewer-checked reference set. Verify each component's hosting and data flow; self-hosted workers or private infrastructure do not automatically make every model call and dependency local.
detail.firstExperiment: Extract a small set of indicators from 30 public project reports and link every returned field to a source region. Measure exact value, unit and reporting-period accuracy together with reviewer correction time before adding synthesis.

scenes.title: Make agent actions observable
scenes.claim: Credo AI now links agents, tool servers and deployment platforms to the use cases that depend on them.
scenes.implication: Define permitted actions, test the complete task and preserve evidence for decisions about deploying an agent.
scenes.watch: Track unauthorized actions, missed failures, recovery time, answer quality and control coverage.

detail.opportunity: An agent's risk depends on the tools, permissions, data and platforms that surround it. Identity, runtime monitoring, task evaluation and dependency-aware governance can make that operational picture easier to inspect, but address different control layers.
detail.proofToSeek: Use a task suite containing stale sources, misleading instructions, revoked access and failed tools to see which controls work. A governance record or vendor policy pack is supporting evidence and does not establish institutional compliance or prove safe behavior.
detail.firstExperiment: Instrument one bounded agent with action traces, least-privilege access and a small regression suite. Map its model and tool dependencies to the use case, then require a reviewer to explain a release decision using the collected evidence.

scenes.title: Scientific AI closes the experiment loop
scenes.claim: LILA reports closed-loop catalyst experiments; other builders connect materials search and engineering models.
scenes.implication: Watch for validated gains in materials, energy equipment and industrial processes that affect development costs.
scenes.watch: Seek independent replication, manufacturing feasibility and performance beyond training conditions.

detail.opportunity: Some frontier builders are moving from predicting a useful design to choosing experiments, learning from their results and repeating the cycle. Others use learned physics models to search engineering designs, creating potential connections to energy systems, materials and manufacturing.
detail.proofToSeek: Separate company-reported research results from replicated performance and manufacturable products. LILA's catalyst report explicitly describes unfinished technology; engineering surrogates also need tested accuracy limits and behavior on unseen conditions.
detail.firstExperiment: Choose one engineering benchmark with a trusted solver or an experimental result that an independent team can reproduce. Compare validated accuracy, total iteration cost and whether the faster process changes the final design or decision.

scenes.title: Physical AI learns in simulated worlds
scenes.claim: Robot policies and world models increasingly connect perception, simulation and physical actions.
scenes.implication: Monitor inspection, logistics and manufacturing tasks where safe, affordable automation could remove bottlenecks.
scenes.watch: Demonstrate repeatable operation, safe failure and total cost in the real deployment setting.

detail.opportunity: General robot policies and simulated environments create new ways to learn and test physical tasks before or alongside real-world deployment. The development connection is strongest where a specific inspection, logistics or industrial bottleneck has a feasible operating setting.
detail.proofToSeek: Request repeated task results under varied lighting, layouts, objects and interruptions, including the failures and human interventions. A visually convincing simulated world does not establish engineering accuracy, and a successful demonstration does not establish affordable field operation.
detail.firstExperiment: Define one task with a safe test area, a clear completion condition and an existing human or conventional-automation baseline. Compare completion reliability, interventions, maintenance and full operating cost before considering a broader application.
